# requireFunction

<link-summary>Returns the value as a function, or throws.</link-summary>

<web-summary>requireFunction() — Returns the value as a function, or throws. apps-script-utils, English.</web-summary>

<tldr>
<p>Module: <code>lang/base</code> · Since: 1.11.0</p>
</tldr>

```typescript
function requireFunction( value: unknown, message: string = "Expected a function." // eslint-disable-next-line @typescript-eslint/no-unsafe-function-type ): Function;
```

Classified by its internal tag, so ordinary, `async`, generator and async-generator functions all pass. A class is a function too.

`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).

## Parameters

| Parameter                                         | Type      | Description                                                   |
| :------------------------------------------------ | :-------- | :------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `value`                                           | `unknown` | The value to validate.                                        |
| `message` _(optional)_ `= "Expected a function."` | `string`  | The message of the exception. A default is used when omitted. |

## Returns

`Function` — the same value, typed as a function.

## Throws

| Exception                  | Condition                    |
| :------------------------- | :--------------------------- |
| `IllegalArgumentException` | the value is not a function. |

## Examples

### What passes and what does not

```javascript
requireFunction(function () {}); // => function () {}
requireFunction(async function () {}); // => async function () {}
requireFunction(null); // throws IllegalArgumentException
requireFunction("fn"); // throws IllegalArgumentException
```
